reason: The cited evidence (E2) directly supports the formation of Cr2O3 and (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 spinel upon thermal exposure at 800°C and states this enhances wear resistance, but the evidence is for a FeCoNiMnCu coating on steel, not FeNiCrCoCu, and does not address friction reduction, adhesion, or the specific temperature/load boundaries claimed.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu coatings in air at 800°C forms a protective oxide layer containing Cr2O3 and spinel oxides
This oxide layer enhances wear resistance
The oxide layer reduces friction by limiting metal–metal contact
The effect is significant under high-temperature (600–800°C) and high-load conditions
The oxide layer adheres well to the underlying alloy
